reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is an instructional walkthrough showing how to access Forsage through Trust Wallet, enter a referrer's link or ID, register, and review the required fees. The material shows a concrete payment-related process, but it does not provide an observable deceptive earnings promise, misrepresent a delivered benefit, or establish that the creator is concealing the destination or money flow.

citations.quote: HOW TO JOIN FORSAGE WITH TRUST WALLET (Quickest method)
The first thing to do is click on the four squares at the bottom.
Then you need to put in the link from the person who referred you to Versailles.
so you click on registration and make sure the ID number is from the person that sent you the link then you click register

opening.argument: This is presented as a business-starting pathway, not merely neutral wallet education: viewers are directed to follow a referrer’s link, verify that person’s ID, register, and have sufficient wallet funds available. The registration flow then leads directly to a payment request for X3 and X4. That sequence links referral-based participation and a financial commitment, making the walkthrough function as a solicitation to enter the Forsage structure rather than an independent explanation of how it works.

citations.quote: show you how you can use Trust Wallet to start your Versailles business
Then you need to put in the link from the person who referred you to Versailles.
make sure the ID number is from the person that sent you the link then you click register

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this an instructional walkthrough does not answer what the instructions are for. The video does not merely explain wallet navigation: it directs viewers through a referrer-linked registration and toward a payment screen. The reference argument also minimizes the significance of the required funds, even though the displayed confirmation associates the transaction with X3 and X4 and shows a network fee.

citations.quote: so make sure you have enough funds in your Trust Wallet to start.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructions establish a registration procedure, but they do not establish that viewers receive income, rewards, or commissions, nor that participation depends on recruiting others. A referrer’s link and an inviter ID can identify who directed a user to a site without proving a downline or tiered earning structure. The payment screen shows a proposed transaction, not a deceptive outcome or promised return.

citations.quote: Then you need to put in the link from the person who referred you to Versailles.

opening.argument: Several concrete signals compound here: the viewer is sent through an external Forsage DApp, told to use a crypto wallet, instructed to confirm an inviter or upline, and told to keep enough funds available before starting. The payment confirmation displays -0.05 ETH for X3 and X4, a 0.06983083 ETH network fee, and a maximum total of $47.36. A registration flow tied to an upline and a substantial additional fee is materially riskier than ordinary software instruction and supports treating the promotion as a recruitment-based scam pathway.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The claim that no deceptive promise is observable overlooks the concentration of risk signals. The viewer is not shown a generic wallet tutorial; the process reaches a Forsage registration page with an upline and then a crypto confirmation requiring funds. The fee is not incidental background: the narration explicitly tells viewers to have enough money in the wallet to begin.

citations.quote: make sure you have enough funds in your Trust Wallet to start.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These signals show a crypto registration and its displayed costs, but riskiness is not itself evidence of a scam. The screen does not show a promised return, a false guarantee, or money flowing to recruited participants. The narrated amounts and visible fee are disclosed rather than concealed, and the transaction is shown as unavailable because of insufficient balance, not as a completed loss.

citations.quote: that will show you the giant fee when you first start

opening.argument: Although framed as a how-to, the material actively lowers the barrier to joining a named referral-linked system. It identifies the wallet route, directs viewers to use the person’s link and ID, explains the registration button, and tells them what balance to keep available. The screen itself labels the participant relationship as an upline and presents a Forsage registration page. That operational detail is promotional because it equips viewers to enter the structure, rather than neutrally reviewing its legitimacy or risks.

citations.quote: HOW TO JOIN FORSAGE WITH TRUST WALLET (Quickest method)
The first thing to do is click on the four squares at the bottom.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The label “instructional” describes the format, not the function. A fastest-method title, step-by-step wallet directions, referrer verification, and a registration payment screen collectively make participation easier. The reference side’s assertion that there is no concealment does not resolve whether the content is steering viewers into an upline-based system.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Operational guidance can facilitate a user’s chosen registration without being a scam promotion. The title and narration describe how to access the service, while the evidence does not show earnings, commissions, testimonials, or a claim that recruiting an upline will produce income. Calling the field “Upline” does not by itself prove a tiered compensation plan or deceptive solicitation.
